_comment: Milestone B trigger registry (bd: shode-roadmap/C-B1, ROADMAP-runtime-10.md SS 3.2; phase vocabulary reconciled bd: shode-roadmap/C-A6 iter0). Every route below is a verbatim transcription of a trigger rule that already exists in prose somewhere in this repo -- no new routing rule invented. See each entry's own `_source` for the exact file. Read by scripts/route.sh only -- NOT preloaded into any agent context. `phases` uses the SAME node ids as references/state-machine/transitions.json's `.states` (e.g. '1a-spec', '3b-review') -- state machine is the single source of truth for phase vocabulary. C-B1 originally used a second, different vocabulary (phase_0/phase_1b/phase_3b/...) borrowed from ROADMAP-runtime-10.md SS3.3's own illustrative example; that was drift (two names for one concept) and is fixed here -- the maintainer suite test-registry.sh now asserts every id used here exists in transitions.json's states[] so it cannot silently drift again. L1 amendment (bd: shode-house-5cs.2, honesty note: 'if you change what a route MEANS rather than how it is matched, say so explicitly'): scripts/route.sh's `text` matcher moved from raw substring (jq contains()) to word/token matching (see route.sh header) -- that part is a pure matching-mechanism fix, no meaning changed. Separately, five single-word `when.any` entries that were themselves ambiguous English words (not just substring-fragile) got NARROWED into multi-word AND phrases -- that DOES change what those five routes mean, not just how they match; see each affected route's own `_disambiguated` field for the specific before/after and why. No route's `_source` prose changed; the underlying domain-selection rule transcribed from prose is unchanged, only the single keyword chosen to detect it in free text got more specific. L1 iter1 amendment (bd: shode-house-5cs.2, after 3-axis review FAIL on iter0): (F1) route.sh's tokenizer now keeps a hyphen-joined run as one token, since a plain [a-z0-9]+ scan made every hyphenated when.any keyword (external-integration/file-upload/ai-agent) permanently unmatchable -- pure matching-mechanism fix, no meaning changed. (F2) a phrase's final word (and any standalone single-word keyword) now also matches its regular plural via a trailing-s stem rule -- restores coverage the old substring matcher had for free, no meaning changed, irregular plurals still excluded (documented gap). (F3) AND-phrase matching changed from 'words present anywhere in text' to 'words present as an ADJACENT run, in order' -- this DOES change what those routes match (stricter): the iter0 'anywhere' semantics reintroduced false positives of the exact shape this bd exists to close (e.g. 'in order to speed up trading of assets' wrongly required plan:trading). (F4) 'exchange' in domain-trading, previously left as a bare single keyword, was judged comparably generic to the five already-narrowed keywords and narrowed to 'trading exchange' -- meaning-changing, same rationale as the original five. L1 iter2 amendment (bd: shode-house-5cs.2, after 3-axis review FAIL on iter1 -- three new defects found in iter1's own new mechanisms, none of them meaning-changing, all pure matching-mechanism fixes): (D1) sentence/clause-terminating punctuation ('.','!','?',',',';', newline) is now replaced with a sentinel word before tokenizing, so 'trading' at the end of one sentence and 'order' at the start of the next are no longer treated as adjacent just because the punctuation between them silently vanished from the token array -- this was a gap in iter1 F3's adjacency check, not a reversion of it. (D2) the plural-stem length floor was raised from >3 to >4 chars after 'this refactor saps my energy' wrongly matched keyword 'sap' (stem('saps')==stem('sap')); every when.any keyword was checked for the same collision shape, only 'sap'/'kyc'/'mrp'/'btp'/'pms' (all 3 chars) lose plural eligibility, none of which had a fixture depending on it. (D3) a second, hyphen-splitting token view is now used for multi-word phrase matching specifically, so a hyphenated spelling of a phrase ('FIX-protocol support', 'trading-order flow', 'insurance-policy renewal') matches the same as the space-separated spelling -- iter1's single hyphen-preserving tokenizer fixed F1 (hyphenated single keywords) but as a side effect made every hyphenated PHRASE spelling unmatchable; both behaviors now hold at once. See route.sh header for the full matching-algorithm writeup and each affected route's own `_disambiguated` field for the specific before/after. L1 iter3/iter3b/iter3c amendment (bd: shode-house-5cs.2, honesty note -- the two paragraphs above describe D1 and D3 as CURRENT mechanisms; they are not, and this note exists because that drifted undetected until a Spec-axis review caught it at iter3b re-review): D1's sentinel-word substitution (replacing sentence/clause-terminating punctuation with a sentinel before tokenizing) and D3's second, hyphen-splitting token view (used specifically for multi-word phrase matching) were both REMOVED in iter3, not merely amended -- neither mechanism exists anywhere in scripts/route.sh any more (zero occurrences of 'sentinel' or a second phrase-token view in the current file). They were superseded by a single positive rule, defined once: two phrase words are adjacent iff the gap between them is EITHER a run of one-or-more WHITESPACE characters OR exactly one ASCII hyphen with no whitespace on either side of it -- see route.sh header's `is_separator`/`$items`/`phrase_match` writeup for the full mechanism. iter3 first shipped this rule matching a whitespace RUN of any length made of space/tab/newline; iter3b corrected iter3's own regression (iter3 required exactly one separator CHARACTER, so an ordinary double-space run was wrongly rejected); iter3c corrected iter3b's own remaining gap (the whitespace half was still an enumerated three-character list -- space/tab/LF only -- so CR, VT, FF, and every non-ASCII whitespace codepoint fell through; fixed by matching the whitespace CHARACTER CLASS instead of any enumerated list, per Oliver's ruling that all whitespace counts, Unicode included). This single positive rule is what is actually running today; D1's sentinel and D3's second token view above are historical record of what iter1/iter2 shipped, not a description of current behavior.

routes._disambiguated: bd: shode-house-5cs.2 -- bare 'stock' false-matched generic code text unrelated to inventory (e.g. a 'stock ticker' UI helper in a refactor task). Narrowed to the AND-phrase 'inventory stock' (both words must appear as ADJACENT tokens, in order -- iter1 F3; earlier iter0 language said 'not necessarily adjacent', which reintroduced a false-positive class, see route.sh header) so a bare mention of 'stock' alone no longer routes here. The phrase's final word also matches its regular plural (iter1 F2, e.g. matches '...inventory stocks report').

bd: shode-house-5cs.2 -- bare 'fix' false-matched ordinary bug-fix requests ('please fix this bug') AND matched as a substring fragment inside unrelated words ('prefix') before the word-token fix in route.sh; bare 'order' is a generic English word ('in order to', 'sort order') unrelated to trading order management; bare 'exchange' is comparably generic ('exchange rate', 'data exchange', 'exchange server' -- iter1 F4, Bella spec review) and unrelated to a trading exchange/venue. Narrowed to AND-phrases 'fix protocol' (FIX the trading protocol), 'trading order', and 'trading exchange' (all words must appear as ADJACENT tokens, in order -- iter1 F3; earlier iter0 language said 'not necessarily adjacent', which reintroduced a false-positive class, see route.sh header) so the generic senses no longer route here. The phrase's final word also matches its regular plural (iter1 F2, e.g. 'trading order' matches 'trading orders') -- see route.sh header 'stem()'. The bare keyword 'trade' is deliberately left un-disambiguated (unlike fix/order/exchange above) and known to collide with unrelated uses (e.g. 'skilled trades', a union/construction sense) -- tracked separately as bd shode-house-b7d, not this bd's scope; do not change the keyword itself here.
